p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Buy a **domain** (your web address) and check that it is free before you pay.
Sign up for Google Workspace (paid business email) on the **$7 per month** plan first, through the pricing page link.
Pick the **annual plan** only if you will keep the account for a full year. Otherwise pick the flexible plan.

Use one main address plus free **aliases** (extra addresses that go to the same inbox) instead of paying for extra users.
Prices change, so check the live pricing page before you sign up.
Use a business email on your own web address. **Google Workspace** with the Business Starter plan is the usual start.
Turn on **two-step verification**, so a new device needs a code sent to your phone.
For one business number, **Quo's Starter plan** at $15 per user per month is enough, and it includes a toll-free number in the USA and Canada.

**Google Voice** costs $10 per month but gives only local numbers.
**Send a test email** before you use the address with suppliers or customers.
Domain: choosing and buying the domain
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Use a ChatGPT thinking model (a mode where the AI thinks longer before it answers) with **deep research** turned on (a
mode where the AI searches the live internet). Deep research checks which domains (web addresses) are actually free. Without it, most suggested.com domains turn out to be taken.
Namecheap is the domain registrar (the company that sells and manages domain names) used in this approach.
It handles the **purchase**, domain privacy (hides your personal details in public records), and DNS records (the settings that tell the internet where your domain points).
Any other domain provider can be used instead.
buy the domain through Shopify (the online store software) if you want everything linked from the start. It costs a few dollars more than an outside registrar such as Namecheap, which is cheaper.
If the domain still does not link after the **DNS records** are updated, take a screenshot of the DNS records together with the exact error message.
Paste both into a ChatGPT thinking model to get troubleshooting help.

Business Starter on the annual plan costs **$7 per user per month**. It is billed monthly. It requires a 12-month commitment. Choose it only if you will keep the account for at least one year.
Business Starter on the flexible plan has no long-term commitment. You can **cancel or downgrade** at any time.
Buy through the **pricing page link**, not the general signup page. The general signup page shows no pricing and defaults to a higher-priced tier.
Start the trial only from the pricing page link. Choose Business Starter at $7 per month and click **Start a trial**.
Business Starter includes 30 GB of pooled storage (one shared storage space) per user, custom business email, and Gemini in Gmail (Google's AI helper inside email).

It comes with a 14-day free trial at no cost (Singapore list).
Check the plan name carefully. Higher-priced plans appear as the default.
Google Workspace starts with a **free trial of at least 14 days**.
p.h: Google workspace: free trial, billing and seats

p.t: Billing (adding a payment method) can be set up during the trial or after it. **No charge** is made before the trial ends. Google sends a notice before the trial expires, so you can leave billing until then.
Billing begins **14 days after signup** on both the annual and flexible plans.
The annual plan is still billed monthly. The monthly charge stays at **$7**. It is not paid up front.
Users can be added or removed as needed. Each user is a paid mailbox, also called a seat or license.
If billing is **never activated**, the mailbox stops receiving mail when the trial ends. Existing messages cannot be retrieved afterward.
Billing setup asks for the billing address and a credit card on file (a card saved in the account).
Google workspace: free trial, billing and seats (continued)
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t:
Create a payment profile with the address and add a credit card on file. Click **Agree and continue**.
Each additional paid user license costs **$7 per month**.

Aliases are not paid users. They do not add to the monthly price.
A Google Workspace account includes up to **30 alternate email addresses** (aliases) at no extra cost.
You still sign in only with the primary address (the main address of the account). Aliases are used to send and receive mail.
Do not click **"buy more licenses"** in the admin panel (the control page for the account) when you only need extra email addresses. Every added license costs $7 per month.
Aliases on the existing account cover multiple addresses without this cost. Add paid users only when an employee needs their own separate inbox.
When only the first account is needed during setup, click **Cancel** on the prompt to buy more licenses.
Creating extra user accounts is not needed during initial setup and can be skipped. Additional team members can be added later from the admin console (the control panel for the account).
Sign up for the **$7 per month plan first**, before creating any other Google Workspace account for the same domain.
p.h: Google workspace: before you sign up

p.t: If a Google Workspace account was created for the domain before you signed up through the $7 per month link, **cancel that account** and sign up again with the $7 plan.
Otherwise, Google will report that the domain is already in use.
Create the business email address **before** signing up for Quo (a business phone app). Quo asks for a business email and uses it to create the account.

The same address is then used to log in to the app.
Google changes the signup steps often. Follow the **current signup screens**, not older guides.
Existing Google Workspace business email accounts keep working. They do not need to be changed after such an update.
Signing up with a domain you already own leaves that domain and any existing website **unchanged**.
Only the mail routing of the domain (where its email is delivered) is connected to Google.
Google workspace: signup procedures
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: **Signup via the pricing link:**

1. Open the Google Workspace pricing page through the course link, not the general signup page.
2. Under Business Starter ($7 per month), click **Start a trial**.
3. Enter the business name, choose **1 for number of employees, and select the region where the business operates. Then click Next**.
4. Enter the contact's first and last name and a personal email address as a backup login. Then click **Next**.
5. Answer **yes to having a domain name. Enter the domain without https:// or www (for example yourbrand.com). Confirm it and click Next**.
6. Set the sign-in address to sales@yourdomain.com, choose a password, and click **Agree and continue**.
7. Select the annual plan (or flexible if you want no commitment). Then click **Try free for 14 days**.

8. Create a payment profile by entering the address and adding a credit card on file. Then click **Agree and continue**.
9. Click **Get started**.
10. At the domain host question (the company where your domain is managed), keep Shopify if the domain was bought through Shopify. Then click **Continue**.
**Signup for a business email domain (Source A, shorter version):**
1. Open the pricing page through the link. Choose Business Starter ($7 per user per month) and click **Start a trial**.
2. Enter the business name, the number of employees (select **just you for a one-person account), and the region where the business operates. Then click Next**.
3. Enter the name of the person setting up the account and a personal email address as a backup for account recovery. Then click **Next**.
4. When asked whether the business has a domain name, answer **yes**. Enter the domain without https:// or www (for example domain.com). Confirm it and click **Next**.
5. Set the primary sign-in address to sales@yourdomain.com, choose a password, and click **Agree and continue**.
6. Select the Annual plan ($7 per month, 12-month commitment) or the Flexible plan ($8.40 per month). Then click **Try free for 14 days**.
7. Create a payment profile with the billing address and add a credit card on file. Then click **Agree and continue**.
Google workspace: signup procedures (continued)
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t:
8. Click **Get started** to begin the domain verification steps (the checks that prove you own the domain).
**Signup with the domain question and admin steps:**
1. Open workspace.google.com (or search for Google Workspace) and click **Start free trial**.

2. Enter the business name as you want it to appear. Spaces are allowed.
3. Select **'Just you'** as the number of employees if you work alone.
4. Select the country where the business will operate, not necessarily where you live.

**The country cannot be changed after signup.** A warning that your IP address (the number that identifies your internet connection) points to another country can be ignored if the selected country is correct.
5. Enter your own first and last name. You become the **account admin** (the person in charge of the account).
6. Enter a current personal email address. Google sends the welcome message there and uses it for account recovery.
7. When asked whether the business has a domain, choose **'I have a domain' and click Next**.
8. Type the domain name without https:// or slashes (for example example.com). Confirm it is the domain to use, and click **Next**.
9. Answer the optional Google marketing questions as you prefer, and continue.
10. Choose the username prefix (support, sales, hello or info). The full address becomes prefix@yourdomain.
11. Create a password of at least 8 characters and store it somewhere secure. Complete the robot check (a test that proves you are a person) and click **Agree and continue**.
12. Click the blue button to continue into setup. Then sign in again with the new address and password.
13. If Google asks you to verify the account, enter your country and phone number. Choose Text message (SMS) or Automated voice call, click **Get code**, enter the code, and click **Verify**.
14. Accept the terms of service and privacy policy.
15. In the Google Admin console (admin.google.com, the control panel for the account), click **ACTIVATE** under Activate Gmail. This step can take up to 60 minutes.
Google workspace: signup procedures (continued)
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: 16. Click **'Sign in to activate'**. Google detects GoDaddy (a domain host) as your domain host. Sign in to GoDaddy if asked, then click **Connect**.
17. Wait while Google verifies the domain and updates the mail settings. Near the end, the screen shows 'Less than a minute remaining'.
18. If you see 'There was a problem updating settings in GoDaddy.com', click **'Sign in to activate' again. If it fails repeatedly, click 'Switch verification method'** and try another method.
19. When Gmail is activated, skip **'Create new users'** for now.
20. Either click **'Set up billing'** now or later. Google emails you before the 14-day trial ends. Billing requires your name, address and payment method details.

21. Click **'Send test email'** to confirm that mail works.
22. Log in to gmail.com with the new business address to access the inbox.

**Signup for a Singapore-based store:**
1. Search for Google Workspace and open the sign-up page with the free trial.

2. **Start the free trial** and choose the Business Starter plan.
3. Enter the business name (the store or brand name) and the domain name.
4. Enter the number of employees (**Just you** for a solo operator) and the region (Singapore in the example).
5. Enter the first and last name of the admin. The person who creates the account becomes the Google Workspace account admin.

6. Finish creating the account. Then use the business email in the Shopify store contact details.
**Signup field notes:**
The sign-up asks for the number of employees. The options are Just you, 2-9, 10-99, 100-299 and 300+. A solo store owner picks **Just you**.
This answer does not block the setup of a single business email address.
Entering https:// or www in the domain field creates a **wrong domain setup**. Enter only the bare domain, such as domain.com.
The domain step appears as 'Does your business have a domain?'. Select **'I have a domain'** if you already own a domain.
Select the buy-a-domain or free page-domain options **only** if you have no domain yet.
Google workspace: connecting the domain's mail (Activation)
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Activation means connecting your domain's email to Gmail (Google's email service).
Activation routes the domain's email to Gmail. In the Google Admin console, go to **Getting started**, then click **ACTIVATE** under 'Activate Gmail for [yourdomain]'.
The step is estimated at 5 minutes, with a possible wait of up to 60 minutes.
If your domain is registered with GoDaddy, Google detects it automatically during Gmail activation and offers an automated connection.

For a larger domain provider, the automated option usually works too.
Smaller providers may not be detected. They need an alternative verification method.
The connection with GoDaddy is confirmed automatically. Google updates the domain's mail settings and then verifies they are in place.
The check can take a few minutes, so **wait on the screen** rather than closing it.
The error 'There was a problem updating settings in GoDaddy.com' is common. It usually means the two systems did not sync.

It is **not a sign of a setup mistake**.
Retry **'Sign in to activate'** before changing the verification method.
Google may ask for phone verification when it detects unusual activity on a new account.

The code can be sent by text message (SMS) or automated voice call.
The phone number is used **only for security**.
The MX record (the setting that tells the internet where a domain's mail is delivered) for your domain should point to Google: smtp.google.com with **priority 1** (the first choice to try).

Once that is set, all incoming mail for the domain is delivered to Gmail.
Any older mailbox or forwarding setup for the same domain **stops receiving new mail**.

Check what is still in use **before** switching the record.
Send a test email in the Google Admin console after verification.
This confirms that the domain's mail routes correctly. Do this before you use the address with suppliers and customers.

**Post-activation checklist (Google Admin console, Getting started page, in this order):**
1. **Set up billing** (5 min)

2. **Send test email** (after Gmail is activated and the domain is verified)
3. **Create new users** (5 min)
4. **Try out Gmail and other apps** (1 min)

5. **Set up your mobile devices** (10 min)
6. **Migrate your email and documents**, importing existing email, contacts and data (1 hr)
7. **Enhance your mail security**, adding protection against spam (junk email) and phishing (fake emails that try to steal logins) (5 min)
Email addresses and aliases
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Use professional addresses on your **own store domain** instead of a personal inbox. Use them when contacting suppliers, and keep using them for customers.
A simple setup uses **three addresses** on one account: sales@, returns@, and firstname@ on the store domain.

An alias is an extra address that delivers to one inbox.
You select which address to send from for each message. You do **not** need to monitor separate accounts.

Aliases cannot be used to sign in to Google Workspace.
Always sign in with the **primary address** (for example sales@yourdomain.com) and its password.
Aliases receive and send mail through that primary account.
Use the **same Google Workspace email account** for Google Search Console (a free tool showing how your site appears in search), Google Analytics (a tool that counts site visitors),

Google Merchant Center (a tool that holds your product list for Google shopping), and Google Ads (paid advertising).
This lets all Google tools connect and share data cleanly.

**Add alias addresses (Source A, first version):**
1. In the Google Workspace admin panel, click the blue underlined name of the sales@ user.

2. In the left navigation, click **Add alternate emails**.
3. Enter **returns** as the first alias. It becomes returns@yourdomain.com.
4. Enter a personal alias using your first name. Adding your last name is also recommended, for example firstname@yourdomain.com.

5. Click **Save** and check that all addresses are listed as alternate emails under the main account.
**Add alias addresses (Source A, second version):**
1. After the welcome screen for the new account, click **I understand**. Then click **Cancel** on the prompt asking to buy more licenses.

2. Open the Google Workspace admin panel and click the name of the primary account.
3. In the left navigation, click **Add alternate emails**.

4. Add the alternate emails **returns and firstname** (for example, the first name of the operator), each created on the store domain. Include the last name in the alias name if it is used for supplier contact.
5. Check that the list shows sales@, returns@, and firstname@ on the store domain. Then click **Save**.
Email addresses and aliases (continued)
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t:
**Add alias addresses (Source A, older 2020 version, same steps):**
1. Open Google Workspace Admin.

2. Click your primary user (sales@yourdomain.com).
3. Select **Add alternate emails**.
4. Add support@yourdomain.com or returns@yourdomain.com.

5. Add yourfirstname@yourdomain.com.
6. Click **Save changes**.
7. Open Gmail and log in as sales@yourdomain.com.

8. Click the **gear icon (the settings button) and select See all settings**.
9. Go to the **Accounts** tab.
10. Edit the display name to your store name.

11. Add additional **"Send mail as"** addresses for support or returns email.
12. Add your personal email as another **"Send mail as"** option.

13. Set replies to send from the same address the original email was sent to.
**Set up sending from the aliases in Gmail (Source A, first version):**

"Send mail as" is the Gmail setting that lets you send from an alias.
1. Click the **gear icon in Gmail, then click See all settings**.
2. Open the **Accounts tab. Under Send mail as, click Edit** next to the sales address.
3. Change the name from the generic account name to the brand name (for example, the store name). Then click **Save changes**.
4. Click **Add another email address**, enter the name and the alias returns@yourdomain.com, then click **Next step**.
5. Under When replying to a message, change the default from "Always reply from the default address" to **"Reply from the same address the message was sent to"**.
6. Repeat steps 4 and 5 for the personal alias firstname@yourdomain.com.

7. Click **Compose** (the new email button), then choose the From address (sales, returns or personal) to send from it.
**Set up send-as aliases in Gmail (Source A, second version):**

1. In Gmail, click the **gear icon**, then click **See all settings**.
2. Open the **Accounts** tab.
3. Under Send mail as, click **edit on the primary address. Change the name to the store name (the name customers should see). Then click Save changes**.
Email addresses and aliases (continued)
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: 4. Click **Add another email address**. Enter the name (for example, Returns - Store Name) and the returns@ address. Then click **Next step**.
5. In the settings for returns@, set **When replying to a message to "Reply from the same address the message was sent to". Then click Next step**.
6. Add the firstname@ address with the first and last name. Then click **Next step**.
7. Open **Compose** and select the From address (sales@, returns@, or firstname@) before sending.
8. Leave **"Check mail from other accounts"** empty. This is the Gmail feature that pulls mail in from other inboxes. The aliases were already added in Google Workspace, so you do not need it.

**Reply and sending mistakes:**
Gmail's default is to reply from the primary sales address. This happens even when a message arrived at the returns or personal alias.
Change the reply setting to **reply from the same address the message was sent to**. Then customers see a consistent sender.

Do **not** add anything under Check mail from other accounts. The aliases already receive mail through Google Workspace.
**Use the account on a phone:**
To use all addresses on a phone, add the account to the phone's email app. Use the primary sales@yourdomain.com address and its password.
Once added, the app can send and receive from all aliases on the account. No separate setup is needed for each alias on the phone.
In any email app on the phone, add an account using the primary address (sales@yourdomain.com) and its password.
Send and receive mail from all three addresses, because the aliases are linked to the same account.
After activation, the business address can be used at gmail.com.

It also works in desktop and mobile mail apps such as Apple Mail or Outlook, by **adding the Gmail account** to the app.
This lets you send and receive on a phone or computer.
Google workspace: branding, apps and overview
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Google Workspace gives you **professional email** on your own custom domain (your own web address,
such as yourstore.com). It uses the normal Gmail look and has an admin dashboard (the control panel for the account owner).
Google Workspace hosts business email on your own domain (your own web address) and is managed through the Gmail interface (Gmail's screens).
The **Business Starter plan** is the recommended starting plan.
Google Workspace gives you a business email on your own domain, plus Gmail, Calendar, Meet (video calls), Drive (file storage) and Docs (documents), under **one paid account**.
It runs the business email address for the store.
Google Workspace gives you business email on your own domain, plus tools such as Drive and Calendar. It is the **usual way** to set up a professional business email address for a store.
After verification (proving you own the domain), **send a test email** in the Google Admin console (the control panel) to confirm that the domain's mail arrives where it should.
Do this before using the address with suppliers and customers.
**Upload a custom logo** in the Google Workspace admin settings so Gmail shows the store's logo instead of the standard Google logo.
Download the logo from your store, upload it under Custom logo under the profile settings of the main account, and click Save.
Older advice (from the 2020s): the **Business Starter plan is recommended for a new store. Buy it through the pricing page link**, because the general signup page does not show prices.
Email tools: filters and scheduling
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Gmail **filters** (automatic sorting rules) can apply labels (tags) and sort incoming emails automatically.
The assistant can then act on messages without you sorting them by hand. Combine these rules with colour-coded priority labels so urgent messages show up first.
Boomerang for Gmail (an add-on for your web browser) can **schedule emails** to send later. It can also send you a reminder if a recipient has not replied within a set number of days.
Use the reminder to track supplier actions that would otherwise be forgotten.
Boomerang's scheduled sending is optional for business email. In the store described, suppliers and customers did not object to emails sent late at night or early in the morning.
The reminder feature is the more useful part for tracking supplier follow-ups.
With Boomerang for Gmail, you can write emails at night and **schedule delivery** for a set time in the recipient's time zone (their local clock), such as 9 a.m. US time.
This shows suppliers that your email arrives during their business hours, for example by scheduling for 9:03 a.m.
**Enable two-step verification** (a second check, such as a code, on top of the password) for all Google Workspace users.
p.h: Security and gemini in Google workspace

p.t: It sends a code by text message when someone logs in on a new device. This protects the account from anyone who obtains the password.
The other optional items during setup, such as the Gemini sidebar and workspace app downloads, can be **skipped** or enabled later.
The Gemini AI sidebar in Gmail (Gemini is Google's AI helper) can summarize emails, draft emails and auto replies, and find information in the inbox.
It is included with the Google Workspace account and can be minimized or closed. It is optional and not required for the email setup.
Gemini in Gmail is included in the **Starter plan** (Singapore list).
Zoho Workplace is a common alternative to Google Workspace for business email with custom domain aliases (extra email addresses on your
own domain).

p.t: Quo was renamed from OpenPhone. The **service, features and price are unchanged**, and existing OpenPhone accounts were moved over to Quo.
For a single store with one business number, the **Quo Starter plan** is enough. A higher plan is unnecessary for this setup.
Toll-free numbers start with **888 or 855**. Google Voice does not offer them, while OpenPhone includes one local or toll-free number in its plan.
Choosing OpenPhone for a toll-free number costs about **$5 more per month** than Google Voice. Choose Google Voice if a local number is acceptable.
Start with the Starter plan of either tool and upgrade only when more features are needed while scaling (growing the business).
Choose a toll-free number, such as an **855 number**, on the Quo Starter plan because it looks more professional on a store website than a local number.
The difference is minor, but the toll-free number is included in the Starter plan at no extra cost.
Business phone apps such as Google Voice and OpenPhone run on a personal phone and computer. Business calls ring through the app so they are recognizable.
Outbound calls (calls you make) placed in the app show the business number, so **no separate carrier plan** (plan from your phone company) is needed.
A business phone number with a companion app can ring on your phone, handle calls, and provide voice-to-text transcription of voicemail (voicemail turned into written text).
It can also route calls to team members at different times of the day as the business grows.

A business phone number from a VoIP provider (a company that makes phone calls over the internet) can ring through that provider's app on a cell phone. Business calls are then easy to tell apart from personal ones.
Landline routing depends on the provider, so **confirm the setup directly** with them.
A phone-forwarding app can route the store's phone number to your cell phone, so customer calls are answered or returned quickly.
It is useful when you **choose higher-priced products** with a phone number on the site from day one.
Quo: Setup and Use
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Quo (formerly OpenPhone) is a cloud-based (online, not tied to one device) business phone system with iOS and Android mobile apps.
It routes dedicated business numbers and messages through your existing smartphone. Incoming business calls are clearly labeled.
Quo is a business phone system with a mobile app that gives a store **its own phone number**. Calls placed through the app show the business number to the other side.
Incoming calls to that number ring in the app, so the owner can still use a personal phone.
Quo's Starter plan includes one business phone number, a choice of local or toll-free, calling and messaging in the US and Canada, and automatic voicemail transcripts.
Quo's calling and messaging for business numbers works in the **USA and Canada only**.
Quo's Starter plan includes business messaging (SMS text) on the business number in addition to calling. Customers and suppliers can write to the same number as they call.

**Sign up for Quo (first version):**
1. **Click the Quo signup link.**
2. Select Try for free.
3. Enter your business email address.

4. Choose the Starter plan.
5. Select your phone number type (local or toll-free).
**Sign up for Quo and install the app (second version):**

1. Open the Quo sign-up page using the link provided.
2. **Click Try for free.**
3. Sign up with a business email address.
4. Answer the setup questions, including the desired phone number. The account is created instantly.
5. Select the Starter plan and **claim the included toll-free number**.

6. Install the Quo app from the App Store on iPhone or from the Android app store, then log in with the same account. The app works right after login.
**Set up the Quo mobile app:**

1. **Download the Quo app** from the App Store or Google Play.
2. Log in with your Quo account.
3. Calls and messages begin working immediately.
Google voice: setup and use
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Google Voice is added to an existing Google Workspace account that was set up earlier with the business email.
It costs $10 per month, is managed in the Google Voice app on phone and computer, and offers only local numbers chosen by area code. **Toll-free numbers are not offered.**
Google Voice works well in the US but **not while traveling abroad**.
Google Voice serves as the business phone line, answered by the VA (virtual assistant, a hired helper who works remotely) during business hours.
Other inbound messages go into the help desk (the support inbox).
On Google Voice, a call recording starts only after the agent (the person answering) **presses a key**, and a recording notice plays to the caller.
Staff often skip this step, so do not rely on Google Voice for consistent call recording.
**Check the consent rules** (laws on whether callers must agree to being recorded) for recording calls in the countries where the store and its callers are located.
**Google Voice setup for a US business number:**
1. Open the Google Voice sign-up page and **confirm you are logged in** to the Google Workspace account created with the business email.
2. Scroll to the pricing section and choose the Starter plan at **$10 per month**.
3. When prompted, select the location and area code you want. The number issued is a local number.
4. **Install the Google Voice app** on your phone and computer to take inbound calls and place outbound calls.
**OpenPhone setup for a US business number with a toll-free line:**
1. Open the OpenPhone page, review the preview of how it works, and check the pricing.
2. **Click Try it free** and create the account. The trial runs seven days, after which the Starter plan costs $15 per user per month.
3. Choose the toll-free number offered in the plan during signup.
4. **Install the OpenPhone app** on your phone and computer to take inbound calls and place outbound calls.
Mighty Call
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Mighty Call is a business phone app for a second number.
Install it on a computer or phone so business calls ring in the app and can be told apart from personal calls.
Mighty Call provides business phone numbers and call handling for stores. At the time of the call, it offered a **50% discount** for the first three months through a promotional link.
Mighty Call provides business phone numbers and call handling. It **replaced Grasshopper** about a year and a half before the call. One reported issue was that it did not work with T-Mobile.

Grasshopper is the alternative.
Mighty Call is a phone service used for the store's call line, chosen over Grasshopper after testing in 2019. It is used to route calls to the business.
Mighty Call was a cloud phone service used in 2019 to provide business phone numbers for online stores.
Mighty Call is a phone system that can route calls to voicemail. If callers hear **two voicemail messages**, the routing logic (the rules that decide where calls go) is set up wrong.
Contact Mighty Call with the exact day and time the problem happens so they can fix the setting.
Mighty Call is a business phone service that sends voicemail transcripts right away, so messages can be read on the go and returned quickly.
Mighty Call with voice-to-text can turn voicemails into emails with a clickable phone number and email link, so you can call or reply in one tap.
Mighty Call is a virtual phone service (a phone number that lives in the cloud, not on a SIM card) with staff in the United States and the Philippines who answer calls at the same time.
It works from any country, so a store owner living abroad can run phone support from the same number.
A virtual phone service with staff in several countries can be used to answer calls from anywhere in the world. It allows a store owner in another country to run the same phone support.
Grasshopper and Aircall
p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Grasshopper provides a business phone number (typically 1-800 format).
It shows this number to customers while **routing calls and texts** to your mobile phone through the Grasshopper app. This keeps a professional identity without exposing personal numbers.
Grasshopper is a virtual phone provider that handles both calls and SMS texting for a business number.
Its **text-back button** sends an automatic message to a caller you missed, saying you missed the call and will respond soon.
Grasshopper is a provider for toll-free business numbers, used when a store wants an **800 number**.
Aircall integrates (connects) with Reamaze (a customer support tool). Each incoming call is **logged automatically** (saved to the record), and the customer's order information appears on screen.
This lets the team handle a call from one platform.
Skype was the most reliable phone solution while traveling abroad.
p.h: Skype, text free and messaging apps

p.t: It was compared with Google Voice, toll-free number forwarding and Grasshopper. Skype is a **workaround for travel**, not the general recommendation.

For SMS or sign-up numbers (numbers needed to create accounts on websites), use a **free second number from the Text Free app instead of your personal phone. The app issues a free number tied to your email.**
**The number stays active as long as you make a call roughly once a month**.
Text-Free was used to get a phone number for a new Ads Manager (the advertising dashboard of an ad platform) **without using a personal number**.
WhatsApp can be used for free calls and messaging with customers, including international calls.

Its encryption (scrambling messages so only the two sides can read them) is a selling point for privacy-conscious buyers. It is common for customers in Europe and can be used alongside an SMS provider.
Business phone numbers for non-US residents can be obtained through options such as MightyCall, Skype or Google Voice.
Open Phone is recommended for Canada-based sellers shipping to the US. If none work, **ask in the community forum**.

p.s: Domain, business email and phone setup

p.t: Use a phone service that sends an SMS or email notification whenever a voicemail is left.
The notification should show the caller's number and let you play the recorded message.
**Divert unanswered calls (send missed calls on) from your business number to a prerecorded voicemail greeting (a recorded message that plays first) through your phone provider.**
**Use a toll-free number such as a US 800 number**, or an Australian 1-300 number if you operate in Australia.
Set up a professional-sounding voicemail for the store phone, either by hiring a voice actor on Fiverr (a freelancer marketplace) or by having a friend record a scripted greeting.
**Avoid using the founder's own voice**, because a third-party voice makes the business look like a larger company.
